question: Does averaging complete40-class probabilities over all context-only alpha permutations necessarily stay in the native head function family with fixed value/decoder/bias?
answer: No, on the admitted head-feature API domain. Uniform mixing restores row-permutation symmetry but can break complete-row replication invariance.
native_family: All mathematical five native normalized pointwise-selector heads are invariant under k-fold duplication of every complete valid(H,R)row, including entity rows/mask. In particular the fixed-U quantum family is.

fixture.features: H_i=e_i in1024 dimensions; duplicate complete H/R/mask rows together
fixture.roles: Two context rows have both membership bits0; subject/object rows have corresponding membership bit1. Roles are arbitrary valid head-API tensors, not asserted to be outputs of the text/role pipeline.
fixture.circuit: Effect angles0. Prepare only first-layer first-wire RY: contextB pi/2 via finite atanh(1/2) coefficient on H_B; all other inputs/angles0. Directed CNOT rings fix|000> and do not map the orthogonal branch to0. Thus q=(1,1/2,1,1).

exact_proof: Every native logit is b_r+sum_i w_ri*u_ri/sum_i w_ri, with pointwise w and u. Complete k-fold row duplication multiplies numerator/denominator byk, so every40-class native probability is unchanged, for every parameter setting.
Uniform context-alpha permutation at replication1 yields logits a,b with probability1/2 each. At replication2 it yields a,m,b with probabilities1/6,2/3,1/6 by choosing2 of4 weight positions.
f(z)=exp(z)/(exp(z)+39). For z in[b,a] subset(0,1), f_second=39 exp(z)(39-exp(z))/(exp(z)+39)^3>0 because exp(z)<e<3<39.

M1-M2=(f(a)+f(b)-2f(m))/3>0 by strict convexity. The full40-vector differs, while every candidate native function gives equal vectors on the two duplicated inputs. Hence no native function matches M on both inputs.

For general replicationk, the count of high weights assigned to thek A positions is Hypergeometric(2k,k,k); z=b+(a-b)J/k, E z=m, Var z=(a-b)^2/[4(2k-1)]. Taylor/Jensen bounds give a cardinality-dependent mixture bias vanishing as k grows. This generic bound is not claimed novel.

illustration.status: Numerical illustration only, not interval-certified proof. Strict inequality follows analytically from f second derivative.

implementation_boundary: No new native model or diagnostic implemented. Existing replay is one deterministic ID/hash permutation and CE comparison, not this hypothetical uniform probability-mixture ensemble. Averaging logits, probabilities and losses are distinct.
scientific_prediction: On these fixed head-API tensors, complete feature-row replication leaves every native mode unchanged, while this uniform probability ensemble changes. This does not distinguish quantum from matched classical heads; it is an interpretation exclusion, not a selectedL5 mechanism.
limits: Exact real-arithmetic head-API claim only; no bitwise floating-point forward or frozenRoBERTa-image realization certified.
No raw-text duplication or semantic label-preservation claim; marked encoder/role extraction can change every feature.
No explanation or rejection of actual fresh5 CE alignment/L4, and no optimizer or task-utility guarantee.
No claim that averaging logits lies inside/outside the native family, no claim for all possible postprocessing ensembles.
